summary: Every stage, bullet and routing target in the retro flow is backed by a line in skills/retro.md; the only softening is that 'can fire' drops the tool-installed condition. The main gap is on the other side: the guardrail paragraph (inspect and cite hook/CI wiring, known-failure lists, mechanical vs judgement) and the per-category proposed remedies are not shown anywhere.

code.overview: Retro is almost entirely agent-followed prose: skills/retro.md is the whole procedure and no script reconstructs a session, traces causes, ranks findings, builds the report or routes the chosen work. The only retro-specific files with any effect are the thin wrappers and the RESOLVER row that make /retro reachable and carry its 'only when the user requests' description. There is no retro test script; the generic skill validator (scripts/check-resolvable.ts) covers its registration like any other skill.

refs.anchor: description: Use only when the user requests a session retrospective to identify evidence-backed improvements to agent tooling, checks, navigation, and steering; present proposals before changes
refs.title: Claude wrapper: retro runs only on request
refs.explain: The frontmatter description begins 'Use only when the user requests a session retrospective' and ends 'present proposals before changes'. The last line includes the canonical body skills/retro.md.
refs.why: The first stage says retro runs only when the user asks for it. This description is the text a harness reads when deciding whether to activate the skill, and the RESOLVER row for retro matches only the literal /retro command. Nothing in code blocks an unrequested run; it rests on this wording. Rebuilding the session from the conversation or a log is done by the agent; no script reads session logs.

promptOnly.what: The agent reads repo instructions, skills, check commands, hooks and CI wiring itself and ties each struggle to an environmental cause.
The agent sorts findings into the category table in the skill, keeps one durable remedy per finding, and ranks by impact, recurrence and cost.
The agent writes the R-01 style table with evidence, cause, proposed change, cost and verification, and makes no edits; the read-only rule is not enforced by code.
After the user picks remedies the agent hands each to the named skill (skillify, add-linter, feature-chain, upstream, improve, code-refiner or prune); there is no dispatcher.
